verdict.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration framework and platform, not itself an agent, so an official MCP server is a fair axis. The first-party Agent Server OpenAPI spec lists MCP endpoints alongside Assistants, Threads and Runs, which indicates the LangGraph runtime itself exposes an MCP endpoint. That evidence is only a single line in an endpoint inventory; the MCPAdapter material describes client-side tool consumption and is not credited here. Missing for 10: documentation of how agents connect to the MCP endpoint, which graphs or tools it exposes, and auth or transport details, plus any hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: covering Assistants ("An assistant is a configured instance of a graph."), Threads, Thread Runs, Stateless Runs, Crons, Store, A2A, MCP, and System endpoints
